verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.73
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 4.73

verses.pali: 8. Apaṇṇakavagga
verses.english: 8.  Sure Bet

verses.pali: Sappurisasutta
verses.english: A True Person

verses.pali: “Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato asappuriso veditabbo.
verses.english: “Mendicants, an untrue person can be known by four qualities.

verses.pali: Katamehi catūhi?
verses.english: What four?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, asappuriso yo hoti parassa avaṇṇo taṁ apuṭṭhopi pātu karoti, ko pana vādo puṭṭhassa.
verses.english: To start with, an untrue person speaks ill of another even when not asked, let alone when asked.

verses.pali: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto ahāpetvā alambitvā paripūraṁ vitthārena parassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
verses.english: But when summoned for questioning they speak ill of another in full detail, not leaving anything out.

verses.pali: Veditabbametaṁ, bhikkhave, asappuriso ayaṁ bhavanti.
verses.english: That’s how to know that this is an untrue person.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, asappuriso yo hoti parassa vaṇṇo taṁ puṭṭhopi na pātu karoti, ko pana vādo apuṭṭhassa.
verses.english: Furthermore, an untrue person doesn’t speak well of another even when asked, let alone when not asked.

verses.pali: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto hāpetvā lambitvā aparipūraṁ avitthārena parassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
verses.english: But when summoned for questioning they speak well of another without giving the full details, leaving many things out.

verses.pali: Veditabbametaṁ, bhikkhave, asappuriso ayaṁ bhavanti.
verses.english: That’s how to know that this is an untrue person.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, asappuriso yo hoti attano avaṇṇo taṁ puṭṭhopi na pātu karoti, ko pana vādo apuṭṭhassa.
verses.english: Furthermore, an untrue person doesn’t speak ill of themselves even when asked, let alone when not asked.

verses.pali: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto hāpetvā lambitvā aparipūraṁ avitthārena attano avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
verses.english: But when summoned for questioning they speak ill of themselves without giving the full details, leaving many things out.

verses.pali: Veditabbametaṁ, bhikkhave, asappuriso ayaṁ bhavanti.
verses.english: That’s how to know that this is an untrue person.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, asappuriso yo hoti attano vaṇṇo taṁ apuṭṭhopi pātu karoti, ko pana vādo puṭṭhassa.
verses.english: Furthermore, an untrue person speaks well of themselves even when not asked, let alone when asked.

verses.pali: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto ahāpetvā alambitvā paripūraṁ vitthārena attano vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
verses.english: But when summoned for questioning they speak well of themselves in full detail, not leaving anything out.

verses.pali: Veditabbametaṁ, bhikkhave, asappuriso ayaṁ bhavanti.
verses.english: That’s how to know that this is an untrue person.

verses.pali: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato asappuriso veditabbo.
verses.english: An untrue person can be known by these four qualities.

verses.pali: Catūhi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato sappuriso veditabbo.
verses.english: A true person can be known by four qualities.

verses.pali: Katamehi catūhi?
verses.english: What four?

verses.pali: Idha, bhikkhave, sappuriso yo hoti parassa avaṇṇo taṁ puṭṭhopi na pātu karoti, ko pana vādo apuṭṭhassa.
verses.english: To start with, a true person doesn’t speak ill of another even when asked, let alone when not asked.

verses.pali: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto hāpetvā lambitvā aparipūraṁ avitthārena parassa avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
verses.english: But when summoned for questioning they speak ill of another without giving the full details, leaving many things out.

verses.pali: Veditabbametaṁ, bhikkhave, sappuriso ayaṁ bhavanti.
verses.english: That’s how to know that this is a true person.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sappuriso yo hoti parassa vaṇṇo taṁ apuṭṭhopi pātu karoti, ko pana vādo puṭṭhassa.
verses.english: Furthermore, a true person speaks well of another even when not asked, let alone when asked.

verses.pali: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto ahāpetvā alambitvā paripūraṁ vitthārena parassa vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
verses.english: But when summoned for questioning they speak well of another in full detail, not leaving anything out.

verses.pali: Veditabbametaṁ, bhikkhave, sappuriso ayaṁ bhavanti.
verses.english: That’s how to know that this is a true person.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sappuriso yo hoti attano avaṇṇo taṁ apuṭṭhopi pātu karoti, ko pana vādo puṭṭhassa.
verses.english: Furthermore, a true person speaks ill of themselves even when not asked, let alone when asked.

verses.pali: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto ahāpetvā alambitvā paripūraṁ vitthārena attano avaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
verses.english: But when led on by questions they speak ill of themselves in full detail, not leaving anything out.

verses.pali: Veditabbametaṁ, bhikkhave, sappuriso ayaṁ bhavanti.
verses.english: That’s how to know that this is a true person.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, sappuriso yo hoti attano vaṇṇo taṁ puṭṭhopi na pātu karoti, ko pana vādo apuṭṭhassa.
verses.english: Furthermore, a true person doesn’t speak well of themselves even when asked, let alone when not asked.

verses.pali: Puṭṭho kho pana pañhābhinīto hāpetvā lambitvā aparipūraṁ avitthārena attano vaṇṇaṁ bhāsitā hoti.
verses.english: But when summoned for questioning they speak well of themselves without giving the full details, leaving many things out.

verses.pali: Veditabbametaṁ, bhikkhave, sappuriso ayaṁ bhavanti.
verses.english: That’s how to know that this is a true person.

verses.pali: Imehi kho, bhikkhave, catūhi dhammehi samannāgato sappuriso veditabbo.
verses.english: A true person can be known by these four qualities.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, vadhukā yaññadeva rattiṁ vā divaṁ vā ānītā hoti, tāvadevassā tibbaṁ hirottappaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti sassuyāpi sasurepi sāmikepi antamaso dāsakammakaraporisesu.
verses.english: It’s like a bride on the day or night she’s first brought to her husband’s home. Right away she sets up a keen sense of conscience and prudence for her mother and father in law, her husband, and even the bondservants, workers, and staff.

verses.pali: Sā aparena samayena saṁvāsamanvāya vissāsamanvāya sassumpi sasurampi sāmikampi evamāha:
verses.english: But after some time, because of living together and familiarity, she’ll even say to her mother and father in law, or to her husband:

verses.pali: ‘apetha, kiṁ pana tumhe jānāthā’ti.
verses.english: ‘Go away! What would you know?’

verses.pali: Evamevaṁ kho, bhikkhave, idhekacco bhikkhu yaññadeva rattiṁ vā divaṁ vā agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito hoti, tāvadevassa tibbaṁ hirottappaṁ paccupaṭṭhitaṁ hoti bhikkhūsu bhikkhunīsu upāsakesu upāsikāsu antamaso ārāmikasamaṇuddesesu.
verses.english: In the same way, on the day or night a mendicant first goes forth from the lay life to homelessness, right away they set up a keen sense of conscience and prudence for the monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, and even the monastery workers and novices.

verses.pali: So aparena samayena saṁvāsamanvāya vissāsamanvāya ācariyampi upajjhāyampi evamāha:
verses.english: But after some time, because of living together and familiarity, they’ll even say to their tutor or mentor:

verses.pali: ‘apetha, kiṁ pana tumhe jānāthā’ti.
verses.english: ‘Go away! What would you know?’

verses.pali: Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṁ sikkhitabbaṁ:
verses.english: So you should train like this:

verses.pali: ‘adhunāgatavadhukāsamena cetasā viharissāmā’ti.
verses.english: ‘We will live with hearts like that of a newly wedded bride.’

verses.pali: Evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabban”ti.
verses.english: That’s how you should train.”

verses.pali: Tatiyaṁ.
